title: Israeli Strikes and Detonations Continue Across South Lebanon
detail: Israeli forces struck Bani Hayyan, the area between Kfartebnit and Nabatieh al-Fawqa, the outskirts of Zawtar al-Sharqiyeh and a valley between Froun and Ghandourieh, while artillery hit Zawtar al-Sharqiyeh, Mayfadoun, Nabatieh al-Fawqa, Wadi al-Hujeir, Majdalzoun and the outskirts of Kfartebnit. Israeli forces later set fire to homes in the southern border town of al-Khiam and carried out a massive detonation in Deir Seryan. No casualties were reported.

media.caption: Israeli strikes and detonations continue across south Lebanon, Sep 25, 2026

title: PM Salam Tells UN Lebanon Demands Full Israeli Withdrawal, State Monopoly on Arms
detail: Addressing the UN General Assembly's general debate, Prime Minister Nawaf Salam demanded Israel withdraw from all Lebanese territory to the internationally recognized border under the 1949 Armistice Agreement and UNSCR 1701, and said decisions over war, peace and weapons must rest with the Lebanese state alone: 'No one speaks on behalf of Lebanon, and no one negotiates for it, except the Lebanese state.' He described the conflict as a war 'imposed upon' Lebanon despite repeated warnings, said it left behind 'a vast humanitarian crisis,' and warned of a security vacuum in the south if no agreement is reached on a force to replace UNIFIL before its mandate expires Dec 31, 2026.

media.caption: PM Nawaf Salam addresses the UN General Assembly, demanding full Israeli withdrawal, Sep 25, 2026

title: Fadlallah Says Hezbollah Open to Political Solution as Feud With Bassil Erupts
detail: Hezbollah MP Hassan Fadlallah said the party and Amal are not opposed to a 'political solution' in the south, favoring 'diplomacy rooted in our rights' and indirect negotiations, but said no reasonable proposal has been offered since the Nov 27, 2024 ceasefire and ruled out 'surrender, submission, or subservience.' The remarks came as a public feud broke out between Fadlallah and Free Patriotic Movement leader Gebran Bassil, who blamed Hezbollah for dragging Lebanon into an 'unnecessary war' that left its base 'destitute, displaced, emigrant and bankrupt'; Fadlallah accused Bassil of lacking 'loyalty' and being 'morally bankrupt.'

media.caption: Hezbollah MP Hassan Fadlallah says the party is open to a political solution in the south, Sep 25, 2026
